one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-06 to 2026-11-04 contains Vicor's Q3-26 report (pattern: 3rd Tuesday of the month, Oct 21 in 2025 and Jul 21/Apr 21 in 2026; one aggregator says Oct 27) and the hyperscaler Q3 capex prints (late Oct). Q3 revenue was already pre-announced twice (>30% seq., >$186M), so the headline beat is priced. What moves the stock: (a) whether management says the VPD royalty is a recurring per-unit stream or partly catch-up, (b) the Q4 guide and backlog (Q2 $380M), (c) product GM recovery from 46.7%. Headwinds: heavy insider selling (Form 144s Oct 1-2; CEO ~$93M sold in 6 months) and reversal risk after +66% from $184 (Sep 16). Tailwinds: momentum and possible further licensee announcements. Net: roughly symmetric around $305.61, median ~$302, monthly vol ~27% (95%/3.5) plus a fatter-tailed earnings component.

bear.story: Q3 VPD royalty proves partly a one-time catch-up and settles near $10M/qtr; licensees source cheaper unlicensed modules (non-exclusive license) and displace Vicor product; AI capex digestion and product GM stuck below 48%; insider selling continues. comps_summary.peer_range: Fwd P/E on calendarized CY2027 consensus EPS 19.4x-56.7x (AEIS low, ALAB high); derived fwd EV/EBITDA 7.3x-68.6x
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: VICR trades at 49.9x CY2027 consensus EPS ($6.12) and ~60x derived fwd EV/EBITDA, near the top of the peer range (only ALAB is higher). We apply 36x to NTM recurring EPS at the horizon (product 30x, royalties 35x in the SOTP): above the 27.1x median but inside the range, below MPWR (42x) and ALAB (57x).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The ~1.3x premium to the median is limited to what should persist through Oct-2027: (1) ~30% of gross profit comes from royalties at ~100% margin, contracted and backed by an ITC limited exclusion order that lasts the patent life (sources 3, 28); (2) 2027-28 recurring EPS growth ~25-45% vs peer median next-year EPS growth ~30%; (3) $446M net cash, no debt. Offsets that keep it below MPWR/ALAB: product GM 47% vs peers' higher margins, Fab-1 capacity cap until Fab-2, customer concentration (10-K: the majority of Advanced Products revenue comes from one or a few customers), undisclosed royalty terms, Federal Circuit/ITC legal risk, and controlling-holder insider selling. Sell-side outperform calls were not used. Forward EV/EBITDA is derived (TTM EV/EBITDA x fwd P/E / TTM P/E, i.e. scaled by consensus EPS growth) because no free source gives consensus EBITDA; GAAP-TTM vs adjusted-forward mixes distort it, so P/E is the primary multiple.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$160 (under the ~$182-184 pre-license-news level of early/mid Sep 2026 and ~48% under today) the market would be saying the VPD royalty is not recurring or licensees are switching to unlicensed module suppliers, and/or product demand and backlog have rolled over with AI capex. Recurring EPS would then be under ~$4.5 and the licensing growth leg of the thesis is broken, not just volatile.

key_uncertainties: Whether the Sep-2026 VPD AI-OEM royalty is recurring per-unit income or partly a one-time past-use catch-up: terms, licensee and rate are undisclosed (sources 6, 17, 22, 23).

One-off vs recurring: the 2025 $45M settlement and the Q1-26 $28.6M litigation payment are one-time; Q2-26 included $15M recognized from a finite $60M 2-year license (vs ~$5M/qtr cash) and a $10.9M tax benefit. These are excluded from capitalized EPS.
The non-exclusive license lets the OEM buy from unlicensed suppliers, so royalties may cannibalize Vicor product sales.
Fab-1 capacity cap until Fab-2 (late 2027/2028) and product gross margin recovery from 46.7%.
Legal risk: the second ITC case final determination in 2027 and Federal Circuit review could widen or narrow licensing leverage.

Defense/aerospace share is not disclosed. The 2025 10-K says only that Brick Products (industrial, aerospace & defense, transportation) were 39.0% of 2025 revenue and Advanced Products incl. licensing 61.0% (source 9); the Q2-26 call says A&D revenue is growing at a 'larger multiple' with key customers (source 3); the Q2-26 10-Q gives no end-market split (source 2).
AI capex cycle: the in-house base case has 2027 customer AI capex +50%, but revisions are pro-cyclical; a digestion year would hit both product and royalty volumes (source 27).
Governance and flow: controlling CEO selling (~$93M in 6 months; insiders ~$410M in 12 months) and ~8% short interest amplify volatility.
reasoning: Facts: Q2-26 revenue $143.4M = product $112.9M + royalty $30.4M; GAAP EPS $1.04 inflated by a $10.9M tax benefit and a $15M upfront recognition of a finite $60M license; product GM only 46.7%; backlog $380M (+145% y/y); $454M cash, no debt. Q3 was then raised twice (to >30% seq., >$186M) on a new non-exclusive VPD license with a leading AI OEM, plus NH sites for Fab-2/3 and a $150M buyback; the stock went from ~$184 (Sep 16) to $305.61. Separating earnings: recurring = product + pre-2026 licensees (~$15M/qtr) + the VPD stream (assumed $25M/qtr in 2027 after haircutting the Q3 amount for possible catch-up); one-off = 2025 $45M settlement, Q1-26 $28.6M litigation payment, Q2-26 tax benefit, and the finite $60M term license (valued separately at ~$0.3/sh residual). Bottom-up recurring EPS $4.97 (2027) and $6.23 (2028) vs consensus $6.12 for 2027 (4 analysts). Peers: 12 AI-power/AI-component names on calendarized CY2027 consensus P/E (median 27.1x, range 19.4-56.7x); VICR is at 49.9x. Fair value $217 (36x NTM recurring EPS at horizon + cash; SOTP cross-check $210) is ~29% below the price; the gap is licensing optionality and momentum that the base case only partly credits. Scenarios bear $135 (30%) / base $250 (45%) / bull $470 (25%) were turned into a lognormal mixture (sigmas 0.45/0.33/0.40), overall log-sd ~0.6, below the 95% realized vol, which was inflated by the 5x run and the June-Sept round trip ($383 -> $182 -> $306). Ladder median ~$245, P(>= $306) ~0.35, P(>= $611) ~0.07. Alternative-lane evidence: Stocktwits 65% bullish with retail frameworks of $275-325 base; GuruFocus/QuiverQuant show heavy insider selling (insiders ~$410M in 12 months, CEO ~$93M in 6 months, no buys) and guru trimming; new Form 144s on Oct 1-2; independent blogs (Stockti, Insider Monkey, INDmoney) flag undisclosed license terms and cannibalization risk; hedge-fund 13F holders rose to 55 (from 42). Defense/aerospace: no disclosed revenue share; Brick Products (industrial, A&D, transportation) were 39.0% of 2025 revenue per the 10-K, and management says A&D is growing faster with key customers. Limits: Reddit blocked fetching and X was not reachable without search scraping; Vicor's careers page did not render job counts, so no job-posting signal; Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage were unavailable (plan/rate limits), so consensus and peer data come from StockAnalysis.com, and peer forward EV/EBITDA is derived. Lane share is 14 of 28 sources (50%) because filings and the mandated 12-peer data are out of lane. No option prices or implied vol were used.
